learning_outcomes.wording: Explain and compare supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning paradigms, identifying appropriate algorithms for given problem types.
Implement data preprocessing pipelines including cleaning, feature engineering, scaling, and encoding using Python (pandas, scikit-learn).
Build, train, and evaluate supervised learning models (regression and classification) using scikit-learn, applying rigorous cross-validation.
Apply unsupervised learning techniques (clustering, dimensionality reduction) and interpret results in a domain context.
Develop reinforcement learning solutions by defining MDPs and implementing Q-learning or policy gradient methods.
Build and train deep neural networks using TensorFlow/Keras, applying regularisation techniques to prevent overfitting.
Evaluate model performance using appropriate metrics, diagnose bias-variance issues, and apply hyperparameter optimisation.
Design and execute an end-to-end machine learning competition pipeline (Kaggle-style), document findings, and present results.

self_study.activity: Compare ML paradigms and justify problem formulations; practise scientific Python with a reproducible environment record.

sessions.title: Data wrangling and EDA
sessions.indicative_topics: Cleaning, preprocessing, feature engineering and exploratory analysis

self_study.activity: Practise cleaning, feature engineering, scaling and encoding; explain training-only fitting and data provenance.

sessions.title: Regression I
sessions.indicative_topics: Linear regression, objective functions, baseline models

self_study.activity: Derive the least-squares objective and compare a cross-validated baseline with fold-local preprocessing.
Analyse polynomial complexity and regularisation using validation curves and bias-variance reasoning.
Explain tree splits and compare classification metrics under imbalance and unequal error costs.
Compare forests, SVM and ensembles under a common validation protocol; justify methodological trade-offs.
Critique leakage and split design; distinguish model selection from independent performance estimation.
Compare tuning strategies under a fixed computational budget and critique feature-importance interpretations.
Compare clustering assumptions, stability and domain meaning across K-means, hierarchical clustering and DBSCAN.
Connect linear algebra to PCA; critique t-SNE geometry and autoencoder reconstruction, including a neural representation prerequisite bridge.
Formulate an MDP and explain Bellman reasoning and the Q-learning update.
Practise Q-learning with recorded seeds and run variability; contrast policy gradients conceptually. Environment choice remains subject to review.
Connect loss, gradients and optimisation in a TensorFlow/Keras MLP; analyse regularisation and validation curves.

sessions.title: Deep learning II
sessions.indicative_topics: CNN, RNN basics, transfer learning and deployment

self_study.activity: Compare CNN/RNN assumptions and transfer learning; evaluate deployment and reproducibility constraints.

sessions.title: Ethics, fairness and explainability
sessions.indicative_topics: Bias, fairness metrics, responsible ML and explainability

self_study.activity: Critique subgroup metrics, uncertainty, explanation limits and data permissions; distinguish societal bias from bias-variance.
Synthesise connections among methods and reflect on formative feedback; this allocation excludes graded presentation preparation and exam revision.
